content.comment_body: Hello, I previously had no issues programming a [product_name] device, but now I can't establish communication with a new, unused [product_name] module ([article_no]) without an SD card installed. I'm using [product_name] V8 and connected via Ethernet. I can see the module and its IP address when online, but whenever I try to download a circuit diagram, check settings like firmware, upload, or start the device—essentially anything under 'tools' / 'Transfer'—either nothing happens or I get a message saying the connected module doesn't support network communication. Not sure if the module is faulty or if I need to install an SD card (the manual suggests it's not necessary). It's quite frustrating. Any suggestions would be very welcome.

You have a [product_name] from the latest series, as indicated by the order number ([article_no]). To operate this module, you need the latest software, [product_name] V8.2. You can download it from the [company_name] website: demo software, upgrades, updates, and drivers. If you're using Windows, check if you require the 32-bit or 64-bit version. After downloading, you'll have a file called 'Setup.exe'—run this as an administrator.
That's why you're the expert—thanks for the help!

analysis.insight_summary: A user encountered network communication issues when trying to interact with a new [product_name] module through Ethernet using [product_name] V8 software, even though the device was visible online. The software indicated that network communication was not supported for the connected module, causing confusion due to successful prior experiences with different hardware and unclear documentation regarding SD card requirements.
analysis.user_expectations: The user anticipates straightforward network programming and compatibility between [product_name] V8 software and the most recent [product_name] hardware, without the need for additional accessories or unclear setup steps.
